i want to start out by saying that for every person that likes something, there are going to be 3 people that hate it. that is very much the case on imdb, as it is also in the world. there are many negative reviews on this movie, going on about how so many things were cut out and out of order and blah blah blah... i, being a huge fan of the books, approached this film with an open mind. i knew things would be cut. i knew it wouldn't be exactly like the book (because if it was, the movie'd be 5 hours long). so i looked at it honestly, and it was really good.

i have had very high expectations for the movies so far, and most of them, i thought, were pretty good. the first and second were charming, the third was great and getting darker, the fourth was good except for its terrible climax(so highly dramatic! voldemort was seriously prancing around like a ballerina!), and i was really looking forward to the fifth. with a new director comes a new way of interpreting j.k. rowling's brilliant series, and david yates did not disappoint.

in order of the phoenix, voldemort has returned, but the only living witness (who isn't a death eater or voldemort) is harry potter. dumbledore and his friends believe this, but the rest of the world is in doubt, especially the minister of magic, cornelius fudge, who is so scared of the possibility this might be true that he's convinced himself that dumbledore is trying to form a secret army against him. in response to this, the ministry sends a seemingly sweet woman named dolores umbridge (who works for the ministry) to teach defense against the dark arts at hogwarts. sickeningly sweet (as shown by how much sugar she puts in her tea) and evil, she punishes anyone who says voldemort is back (and severely). because of this notion that dumbledore is making up an army of students against the ministry, umbridge won't teach the students in her classes how to do spells, so as to make a "safe, risk free environment". harry's friends then convince him to start a secret club where he can help students learn practical defense against the dark arts to prepare themselves for the wizard war that lies ahead. meanwhile, voldemort is in search of a "weapon" that he needs to reach his goal of wizarding world conquest, and harry's having very strange dreams about a mysterious hallway...

now that that's out of the way, i'll talk about the acting, and wow, was it good. daniel radcliffe is fantastic as harry. he's really developed into a great actor and showed a lot of emotional range in this one. rupert grint and emma watson portray their characters great too - emma's really grown up and rupert's not just comic relief anymore. evanna lynch (who plays luna lovegood) is fantastic and is absolutely perfect for the role - strange, wise and mystic. imelda staunton was a perfect umbridge - she made us love to hate her, and especially to hate her pink cardigans. jason issacs as lucius malfoy was fantastic - he really gave me the shivers, as did ralph fiennes who was a truly terrifying voldemort. michael gambon was great in this one as dumbledore - his way of portraying dumbledore was just right for this one. as always, alan rickman continues to be a perfect snape, and gary oldman as sirius was fantastic too. helena bonham carter proved to be a great bellatrix lestrange - wild, insane, and scary. for the cast, i give the cast a 10 out of 10.

the story was a bit distorted at times, and some things were left out, but overall i really enjoyed it. the climax was changed quite a bit, but in a way, almost for the better. it's strange that the longest book turned out to be the shortest movie, and i think they could have afforded to keep some of the scenes from the book. i was a bit disappointed that none of the quiddich scenes were included in the film and that we saw drako malfoy so little. i found that some parts were a bit unclear, especially to people who haven't read the books. the script strayed a bit from the story, but they kept all the important things. i'd give the script a 7.5 out of ten.

the sets were amazing, especially the ministry of magic sets. 10 out of 10. the effects were superb. i couldn't believe that everything in the prophecy room was cg! everything looked real and amazing, especially *spoiler* the battle between voldemort and dumbledore - it was done beautifully and was epic. 10 out of 10 for effects. the music wasn't as good as the other films, but gave more of a sense that things were getting darker and that it was the real world, so music gets an 8 out of 10. cinematography was absolutely gorgeous. 10 out of 10.

overall, i definitely think that ootp is worth seeing. with a stunning cast, amazing effects, and everything else, this was a really great, entertaining movie. i was on the edge of my seat the whole time! 9 out of ten, just because i wish they'd included the quiddich scenes.

in the previous film in the harry potter series, goblet of fire, revered headmaster professor dumbledore (michael gambon) says, "dark and difficult times lie ahead". in order of the phoenix, they've certainly delivered on his prediction.

in my opinion, one of the main reasons for the success of the potter films has always been the culmination of a intelligent and committed crew with a exceptionally talented cast. on these terms, phoenix met all of my expectations, delivering sterling production values along with a great deal of soul and energy emitted from the terrific cast.

there are some moments which may disappoint or confuse viewers, but not so many as to leave you with a sour taste in your mouth. for viewers who haven't read the books, some plot points might be a little tricky to follow, but there aren't many of these moments, and you can easily catch up with the story during later events. some characters may not have much screen time, but with excellent supporting actors such as david thewlis (professor lupin), brendan gleeson (mad-eye moody), alan rickman (professor snape) and helena bonham carter (bellatrix lestrange) on board, they won't feel underwritten, at least until you've finished watching the film.

the team which deserves the most praise for this wonderful film is the team of director david yates, writer michael goldenberg and star daniel radcliffe. they have channelled all of their efforts into making this a sleek, efficient and tremendously entertaining film for both book and film fans alike. yates, in particular, does an astonishing job, seeing as this is his first motion picture, directing with great skill and visual flair.

goldenberg has written a superb screenplay, which delves into the characters (especially harry and his godfather, sirius black), producing complex, heartfelt and compelling results. although he has missed out elements of the plot which would have made the story clearer, he mostly constructs a fluid and gripping story. he also includes several good moments of humour, which help to counter the growing darkness which leaks from almost every scene.

radcliffe delivers a brilliant performance as the titular wizard. harry's situation may be more fantastical than normal events, but radcliffe's main skill is that he never lets the character slip into fantasy mode, acting with an incredible weariness and humanity. his character makes mistakes, and he has to deal with their consequences. in other words, this is radcliffe's best performance in the series, and probably the best performance of his career so far.

indeed, some of the most impressive moments in the film aren't the excellent wand battles or the moments which are based around the visuals, but the more quiet scenes. two grand examples are the tapestry room scene between harry and sirius (which was extremely moving), and the moment near the climax of the film which sees harry being tortured by voldemort within his mind, which packed intelligent and haunting power. it is scenes like these which provide the necessary emotional link to the hero, and that is why they are so compelling.

the rest of the cast also delivers. alongside radcliffe, rupert grint and emma watson give great performances as ron and hermione, gary oldman brings sirius black (my favourite character in the books) to powerful and charming life, jason isaacs as lucius malfoy, bonham carter's character and ralph fiennes as voldemort make superb villains and imelda staunton is utterly despicable as dolores umbridge, a political messenger who attempts to take over the wizard school of hogwarts.

visually, the film is stunning. all of the creations are utterly convincing and well conceived (except perhaps grawp, a childish, muddy giant who is a little too cute for my tastes). the spells that the pupils and adults use have a great range, from spells which cause light to spring from wands to spells which cause imminent death. there is also some cracking action, which i will not spoil for you.

overall, order of the phoenix is a tremendous achievement, and one of the best films in the series thus far. if you haven't seen it by now, seek it out immediately!

the order of the phoenix was a wonderful representation of the fifth installment to the harry potter series. unlike its predecessor, which was a bit choppy at the beginning, it flowed a lot better, making the movie less confusing for the audiences who didn't read the book.

one great part of the movie itself was the casting of natalia tena (tonks), imelda staunton (dolores umbridge), evanna lynch (luna lovegood), and helena bonhan carter (bellatrix lestrange). each actess was an almost exact impersonation of what i believed to be them.

due to the lack of time for film, there were some developmental issues that could have been useful to comprehend. one example was that tonks's power was never stated in the movie, so her facial transformations were a bit confusing.

staunton made me "love to hate" dolores; lynch made me laugh; and carter wonderfully made lestrange a feared character.

overall, harry potter and the order of the phoenix was a great movie

at 2 hrs and 18 mins. this is actually on the short end of runtimes for 'potter' films, but delivers plenty of bang for the buck. the dursleys make a reappearance, the angst from the 4th film continues, and the wizarding world is in plenty of uproar over whether or not voldemorte is really back. harry and dumbledore endure repeated attempts to sully their word as the ministry for magic asserts the dark lord has not returned. a special group of wizard, the order of the phoenix, knows better and rescues harry from privet drive after a surprise dementor attack. once at hogwarts, only a handful of students believe harry and dumbledore while the rest openly mock him or keep their distance. harry meets luna lovegood, a classmate who has seen death like him and so can see magnificent flying beasts called thestrals. but also on the scene is dolores umbridge -a ministry hack under cornelius fudge who interferes at hogwarts and replaces dumbledore at the school when her strict rules and underlings discover harry has been teaching other students how to defend themselves against the dark arts. however, harry has also been plagued by mental contact from voldemort. snape has been trying to teach harry the skill of occulemency to block these invasions but harry continues to see visions including an attack on arthur weasley and a faked attack on sirius black to lure harry and his friends into the department of mysteries so he can retrieve an orb of prophecy regarding him and voldemort. a battle ensues between the children, the death eaters, and the order of the phoenix climaxing with sirius's death and dumbledore's reappearance to defend harry from voldemort and bellatrix lestrange (murderer of nevelle longbottom's parents).

of course there's an enormity of material in the book that doesn't make it to the movie. some scenes that do make it in include harry's half-hearted courtship with cho chang and the weasley twins' celebrated escape from hogwarts while umbridge is control, and a few others. all-in-all, i think the movie did an admirable job with the volume of material it had to pack into a feature length film. can't wait for the next two!

i know i'm suppose to read the books first but the movies are great. i know they take a lot away from the books, but this 5th installment of the harry potter films was great, i enjoyed the movie the cast is back the only difference is grifindore new character added but he did took it seriously though, good continuation of the saga. i like that this films are getting darker every film that they are showing us and that's the beauty of every harry potter movie so for this being a great franchise and loving every movie that they have done, i give "harry potter and the order of the phoenix" a 9 out of 10 stars.

i watched this movie before i read the book, once i got done with the book i did notice things missing. but that doesn't change the fact that this movie was still brilliantly made. yes the reason so many things were taking out was due to goldbergs screenplay (but if j.k. rowling. approved it then i am sure there's a purpose for the missing material) however, david yates is what made it brilliant, everything he had the actors do was fantastic and i think it is one of the best harry potters yet. one thing i didn't like about the movie was the fact that the book was so long but the movie (although still a good time) did seem rather short. but the effects that were produced and the final 20-30 minutes of the movie were just breathtaking. i recommend this for anyone who is into fantasy movies, whether you like the harry potter series or not. this is still just an amazing, interesting, breathtaking movie that will keep you wanting more.

my first piece of advice is the same as it would be for any other cinematic adaptation of a book. read the book before you watch the movie. there are a couple things (who sent the dementors after harry, why fudge refuses to believe voldemort is back, etc.) that are never fully explained in the movie. for anyone who didn't read the book and wants to know umbridge sent the dementors after harry in an effort to discredit him. as for fudge: he is, to use dumbledore's words, "blinded by the love of the office" he holds. voldemort being back would seriously jeopardize the power he has as minister (not to mention that the idea of voldemort's return is just too terrifying) so he simply ignores the facts.

i was very worried that a lot of events that are so important to the book would be written out of the movie. however, the use of daily prophet headlines/articles to show not only the passage of time, but the happenings around the trio was fantastic! yes, firenze was mostly written out as no one resumed the teaching of divination after professor trelawney was sacked. yes, poor dobby was written out again. the only moment with percy (who is on fudge's side in the book) is a split second glimpse of him standing behind the minister. but - in spite of all that it worked! the pacing was great, there were no dull moments, you still got to see regular teenage moments (i.e. harry & cho's kiss) in between danger and heroism.

the only "major" change of which i do not approve is having neville find the room of requirement. as the chamberpot conversation between dumbledore and harry was written out of goblet of fire there was no advance knowledge that this room existed. as dobby was written out he couldn't be the one to tell harry about it. i think we were supposed to believe that neville was fleeing from bullies and needed a place to hide so the room opened, but it just didn't work. it had a very, "ho-hum look what i found" feel. meh.

i loved the exit of the fred & george. i loved grawp's little crush on hermione. i loved loved loved luna!!!! she was perfect! on the whole it's the best hp adaptation yet and was a great, fun, thrilling, tense ride.

well done!

harry potter and the order of the phoenix is one of the best harry potter films, a very close second to the prisoner of azkaban. here is an exciting fantasy film, with the darker elements of harry potter being brought to the screen, and has additional character depth.

lord voldemort (ralph fiennes) had raised once again and he starts recruiting his forces. he is able to send dementors to attack harry (daniel radcliffe) and his cousin dudley (harry melling), where harry is forced to use the patronus charm. the ministry of magic expel harry from hogwarts and an enquiry is launched. harry discovers that the minster for magic cornelius fudge (robert hardy) denies that voldemort has risen, fearing the backlash and started a media campaign against harry and dumbledore (michael gambon). after harry is saved by dumbledore, fudge sends his loyal employee dolores umbridge (imelda staunton) to serve as hogwarts' new defence against the dark arts teacher. the aim is to undermine dumbledore, and spread ministry propaganda. she is a horrible woman, sickly sweet on the outside, but has no problem torturing students and harbours 'racist' thoughts about non-humans, like centaurs. the ministry aims to avoid teaching practical magic, so harry, hermione (emma watson) and ron (rupert grint) form their own class to teach students, calling it dumbledore's army. harry shows that he is a good teacher. the classes also gives harry a chance to get close to the lovely cho chang (katie leung); but both still suffer from guilt of the death of cedric diggory. harry also suffers nightmares and imagines involving voldemort. he is aware voldemort wants something from the ministry and wants to stop him. snape (alan rickman) tries to teach harry have to block the imagines.

after mike newell left the director's chair, a number of directors were approached, jean-pierre jeunet, michael vaughen and mira nair. in the end david yates was picked to direct, a man who proved himself on british television, and has a nack for the darker elements of life. he ends up being a good fit for the series, showing a good hand with the special effects, brought in his own vision style (e.g. the newspapers), kept the film well paced, had an exciting eye for wizarding battles and shown to be good at casting. this was a very dark film, with deeper themes about politics, the media, and the psychology of grief and isolation. he is one of the best directors the potter series had and he is the man who is going to finish the series. as well as the main cast returning showing their talent, there are new additions. imelda staunton was good as sickly umbridge, and evanna lynch shows she is a promising young actress. helena botham carter was perfect casting as the psychotic bellatrix lestrange; she is one of my favourite actresses. gary oldman is given a lot to do and shows why he is one of the best actors around. radcliffe brings out the fact harry becomes an angry and isolated teenager, wanting to fight but unable to do much about it. ralph fiennes does not have much screen time, but still shows what a great villain he is. he plays voldemort also like the emperor from star wars: return of the jedi.

this is the only potter film that was not written by screenwriter steve kloves. michael goldenberg is given the tough task of adapting the longest harry potter books, and one of the most entertaining into a film. he does it and somehow with david yates makes the shortest potter film. he is forced to cut subplots like the quidditch matches and the scene at st. mungo's hospital, but the key plot reminds and he keeps the dark tone of the film. out of all the potter films this is the most serious (and i like that). i do however criticise the changes to the harry and cho relationship, i would have liked to have seen more of that.

very enjoyable fantasy.

i enjoyed this much more than the last film. i have read the books and as ever i would have done things a bit differently but this is a good movie for anyone who is a harry potter fan.

the usual suspects return to hogwarts for their 5th year to continue their schooling but this time the film concentrates far less on this. harry and his friends once again battle against lord voldermort producing fight scenes which lived up to my expectations, with the final fight a spectacular battle.

i love the way rowling wrote these novels with each one becoming less of a children's book to keep in line with her readers as they became older and this has been reflected well in the movies.

if your a potter fan you will have already seen this and i hope like myself you enjoyed it. if your not a potter fan, why not?

when i saw the last harry potter film (goblet of fire) i was incredibly disappointed, i found the performances of the characters slightly strained and it seemed more interested in showing the action of the triwizard tasks rather than the underlining plot. so i went in to this film expecting much of the same thing. but by god i was in for a surprise. for starters the music to the film was far more grown up, giving the mood of the film its dark atmosphere as it is felt in the book. but by far the best part of the film was the performances of daniel radcliffe and the cast. they all really came into their own, the characters were finally true to the books. i especially loved luna lovegood, i thought the acting was bang on the spot by emmerline vance. i did however think that bellatrix could have had a bigger speaking part but understand that timing in the film would have been an issue. like in the last film i found it dragged on far to long. i also think that umbridge could have been slightly more nasty, as i didn't quite feel the hate reaction that is felt when reading the book. many hints were also dropped during the film that true die hard fans will pick up immediately, it makes me smile how jk rowling has put these in as a tantalising glimpse of what can be expected in deathly hallows. so all in all it is a must see for any harry potter fans, but if you are new to harry potter, it is probably best that you read the book first, as i fear you may get rather bored as plot line is the key part of this film, rather than constant action like the previous film. i cant wait for deathly hallows, and the next film. so, enjoy the film, bibi xxx

although many will disagree, i believe that this harry potter film was the greatest one yet. i've grown up in the harry potter craze, with both the books and the movies. many people are complaining that the fifth installment to the series "left out way too much" and "skipped a huge part of the book!" i have a different point of view than these people. i thought that the movie flowed very nicely, and that they didn't leave out anything 'major' or that will play a greater part in the sixth and seventh movies. i talked to my friend, who does not read the books, although she enjoys the movies, and says that it made sense to her, even though it wasn't as packed as the book was. overall, i'd say this movie was fantastic. not only did it flow nicely, but the younger actors greatly improved. daniel radcliffe (harry potter) really stood out (obviously, because he's the main character), and did an excellent portrayal of all the different emotions and pains harry felt as described in the book. this movie was the best, by far, and all those who are complaining fail to see the greater aspects of the movie.

harry potter movies are the guiltiest of guilty pleasures. they aren't brilliant by any degree, but they are so freakin' entertaining and engrossing they have me on the edge of my seat like a pre-pubescent school girl. yay! 'order of the phoenix', by...(read more) far the most captivating of the five movies, is completely satisfying from beginning to end. the entire cast is back for this installment and all are great as always. the stand-out of course is academy award nominee imelda staunton (vera drake, chicken run) who is absolutely delightful as the ruthless hogwarts teacher who always has a giddy smile on her face. my only complaint with these movies is the fact that harry potter never loses. the movies never have an unhappy ending, and life isn't like that. i hope the next movie ends with harry potter defeated. not dead, but just in a bad situation. they did it in the star wars saga with 'empire strikes back', why can't they do it with this? what kinda message does that teach kids. that no matter what the good guys always win. pbbt! that's bullshit, if you teach your kid that you shouldn't be a parent. anyway, enough of my little bitch-fit rant, all in all 'harry potter and the order of the phoenix' was a wholly enjoyable film that any fantasy movie fan could appreciate. will the next one be better? i dunno, i don't read the books. grade: a-

beginning, the movie is exciting, when harry en dudley get attacked by dementors. and the excitement doesn't stop there: the whole movie is full of exciting moments, flashes, lines and whatever more literally, but also in their acting) and i'm not surprised about the great reviews of order of the phoenix. gary oldman (sirius black) is obviously fantastic: his way of talking/doing things is almost this part (too restless, much more different than richard harris was, he was always more like i had dumbledore in mind), i sort of changed my mind today. he's an outstanding actor and has a very after the first 15 minutes, i could sense that this wasn't going to be like the other hp movies. this one has a dark, gloomy mood about it which isn't helped by harry's frequent temper outbursts. as dumbledore put it towards the end of goblet of fire (hp4) "dark and difficult times lie ahead", so this installment says it all. that means that for harry, ron and hermione and their friends it's no longer enjoyment and pleasure as usual.

however, despite the dark mood of the film, it was great entertainment as the main actors have shown that they have matured with experience. radcliffe, despite his dark moods, has matured with his age and shows that he could be a great star in future. grint is no more the usual inferior ron but has also matured with his age. and watson? she simply gets better and better and is now growing into a real english rose with her looks. ralph fiennes (who i regard as a very handsome guy in reality) looks better as voldemort and meaner too. matthew lewis is more assured as neville and bonnie wright is also making her character ginny more likable.

as for the new characters, imelda staunton is really mean as umbridge and played her so well and i think that helena b. carter was quite good as bellatrix lestrage. but for me, among the new characters the one who really stands out is evanna lynch, who plays luna lovegood. lynch is as pretty as the character she plays and i think she portrayed luna almost exactly as rowling described her. i believe she can get better in the next hp movie.

i heard people complaining that the film was not exactly true to the book and, in truth, i have a few complaints. but it doesn't take anything from this movie. the complaints of most people are mainly that several scenes in the book were omitted from the movie and not that the acting was terrible. if the acting was terrible then i would have cause to complain. but it wasn't and that's what makes this installment tick. for those of you who are complaining, you should not have expected everything in the book to be cramped into the movie, otherwise we may have gotten a 5-hour-long bore instead of a 137-minute flick. see the movie as a movie that it is and you will enjoy it. but if you are going to whine about the plot, then here's my verdict: if you think that because of the omissions, this movie is rubbish, then no movie (and i mean none at all!!) will make you satisfied, and you should not waste your time to watch any movie at all!! because i know that several good movies in the past have thin plots.

overall i give it a 9/10 and despite the dark atmosphere, there is a lot about it that is worth remembering. and that's great!

"harry potter and the order of the phoenix" may have a few story faults more to do with the screen writing change than anything else, but it is nonetheless one of the better films of 2007. comparatively, it is very well-directed and well-acted by the cast, even if the length makes cameos out of every actor except harry, ron, hermione, and umbridge. it does not deserve the nit-picking it has received by fans of the books and snooty critics who want to find some loose thread in the film series to unravel.

it would seem that critics want to fault the series for trying to move in a darker, more mature and character-driven direction, even though that is exactly where the books are going and nothing can change that. critics who don't read the book series have it in their heads that the films should stay light and fluffy and child-friendly and sugary-sweet for some reason, and so as this film maintains the themes of aggression, depression, suppression, and isolation present in the book, the critics aren't happy because this film lacks the whimsy of the prior stories and isn't "fun" anymore. well as snape says in the film, "life isn't fair." the rest of the series only gets darker and more threatening. rowling has written a book series which takes harry's magical world seriously; it mirrors our own world. as the films continue and harry gets older, his awareness of his world increases as he finds people can be insane (bellatrix lestrange), insensitive (snape), or deadly (voldemort) as in the muggle world, but there are also those persons dear and friendly to us, as the weasley family proves.

then there are those recently dubbed "potter nazis" who behave as though they are the protectors of the potter books and act as though the films have debased and decimated the stories, and criticize the films as though it would be quite easy to make a seven-hour film including every little moment from the books. these are unreasonable and oftentimes ignorant people who do not understand how a film is made, nor the necessity of separating the book from the movie. the movies follow the books very closely in tone and style, and apart from omissions and the cutting down of certain characters and scenes, none of the films have ever strayed so far from the books that one could think rowling has lost her control over warner bros. the films stay to the books and rowling approves the script so that future movies are not tangled up.

"order of the phoenix" is perhaps the most annoying of the harry potter books because most people hate how harry and umbridge act. there is so much talk and setting up for the final two books that the book is rather a job to read. this film, however, manages to focus on two key aspects of the book and requires characters and events to revolve around these two threads: a) the ministry of magic's denial of voldemort's return and the actions they take against harry and dumbledore, and b) harry's fears that he is becoming "bad." therefore, a tight story is extracted for the audience to attach itself to. it is highly character-driven for harry as we understand the pain he is going through following the previous film's story, and as we see a new story unfolding which sets harry up with a link to voldemort.

unfortunately, the screenwriter did include dialogue and scenes without giving reason for their inclusion. certain things are seen or said that the audience will have "what's going on?" moments if they pick up on these inconsistencies. they are few and far between, however, and not so terrible that they make the whole movie collapse. and admittedly, as a fan of the harry potter books, it would have been nice to see more of the ministry battle with a few more scenes from the book.

otherwise, the film stays strong with it's solid acting, particularly from radcliffe. the possession scene at the end of the film is heartbreaking and he nails the character's feelings of isolation and depression. keep watch for his inspired neck twisting, it's a key to his character's development in the film. rupert grint also has a new flavor of maturity in the film, which is very welcome. it's all about subtlety for the boys. emma watson, on the other hand, still acts with her eyebrows.

imelda staunton steps into the role of defense against the dark arts teacher this time around, making a splash as the loathed and cringe-worthy toad of a woman. she gets under your skin with every sentence and adds a little salt to make it burn. she is particularly vile and sadistic and makes snape seem huggable. and speaking of snape, alan rickman is absolutely perfect as severus snape, appearing for less than ten minutes of screen time but impressing with just the right amount of sarcasm and malice in his voice. rickman has always played snape straight from the book, but has never been allowed the twisted wit his character is known for. this time around, rickman treats the audience to that flavor of witty disdain for harry.

to close, it is best to acknowledge that michael goldenberg who wrote the screenplay will not be returning as steve kloves has penned the screenplay for "half-blood prince." as a veteran of the harry potter films, kloves will have no problem in adapting the sixth book as it's perhaps the most film-friendly in its plot, and the audience can expect a much more intense and mysterious film. it's a mindtrip of a story and those who maybe lost interest in the potter films after "order of the phoenix" should reconsider: "order of the phoenix" seems like a decline in the series, but i can guarantee "half-blood prince" will surge back as the best in the series, just on the strength of its story.

also the acting was extremely good especially from daniel radcliffe- although it was hard to watch him as he i saw him in equus...

anyway, the special effects were brilliant the fight scene was extremely powerful one thing i was disappointed on was sirius' death. in the book i remember reading that part and absolutely sobbing my eyes out - the film really didn't provoke emotion at this point as it happened rather quickly.

however my favourite quote has to be when ron calls someone a "toss bucket", pure class and english teenage slang which really hasn't been seen in the films before and appealed to me a lot ha i would recommend watching this peoples!

the fifth installment in the harry potter movies is a satisfying retelling of it's book counterpart. what most impressed me was just how much the cast has grown as actors. all of the main characters have improved dramatically and the newcomers, such as beatrice lestrange, were all well chosen for their roles. there is also enough new content to hold the interest of those who have read the book many times over. the new content also succeeds in advancing the story and filling in holes created by missing story elements (elements that were present in the books). i was also really impressed with the way the movie treats the character of dolores umbridge, i was nervous that she would appear too silly in the movie, but she is really well done. all in all, my favorite harry potter movie so far!

let me just say that i have been constantly impressed with the work that is done by the harry potter movies' cast and crew. their improvement has shone brightly throughout the saga. i was especially impressed with the scene at the ministry of magic where sirius is killed. daniel radcliffe's emotion is fantastic and the music and sound editing is spot on. i love how its in slow motion and mute for part of the scene, and then transfers smoothly into sound and movement. i also was impressed in a scene shortly after that where harry is being possessed by voldemort and he is laying on the ground, watched by dumbledore. yet again, daniel radcliffe provides emotion and dynamics.

i was thrilled by the choice of imelda stauten for dolores umbridge. her sickly sweetness is overcast by her love for torture and hate for children. yet again, a spotless performance.

i am also continuously impressed by the music soundtrack. the songs add dimension and feeling to every scene.

all in all, i feel that the great legend of harry potter is perfectly portrayed in its movie counterparts.

after the events of the goblet of fire, harry and dumbledore are said to be lying about the return of voldemort. this causes the ministry to lose faith in dumbledores ability to be the headmaster at hogwarts. to correct what the ministry believes to be a failing wizardry school, they place dolores umbridge as the defence against the dark arts teacher, in hopes that she can correct the school.

this film is great and the direction of david yates corrects all of the tone issues that goblet of fire had. this time around yates brings a different feel to the franchise but one that makes sense with the story being told. it's dark when it needs to be but it also has that magical feel in the scenes that it's needed. for example at the beginning of the film when the dementors come, we get a really dark scene that shows where this franchise is going, but not long after we get a scene where harry is in aw as a building opens up to reveal the headquarters of the order of the phoenix.

as per usual the cast is back and is across the board flawless. daniel radcliffe is back as harry potter and we get to see harry take on this new role of a teacher as he attempts to correct the teaching done by dolores umbridge. this is a really cool story for harry because of how good he is at being the guy these other students look up to, they rely on harry to teach them proper magic and the film shows harry's leadership capabilities. it also creates for a lot of great training montages that show the development of these students abilities.

the new addition to the franchise is the amazingly despicable character of dolores umbridge played by imelda staunton. dolores begins creating way over the top rules that are putting a strain on the enjoyment of being at hogwarts. her character is so well written, she is this insanely bad person but you can't help but stay locked in whenever she is on screen and towards the end when harry and hermonie trick her you can only feel joy as she is swept of by the minotaurs.

we also get a really cool new character in the form of luna lovegood. her character is really quirky and different from the other students but that's what makes her so great.

although dolores being at hogwarts is a big issue for these characters, this story was building up to something greater the conflict between the death eaters and the order of the phoenix. this third act sequence of harry and the others fighting the death eaters is our first real showing of what a wizard fight looks like, and it was insanely well done. the battle eventually gets to a fight between dimbledore and voldemort in an amazing fight scene showing the true strength of each of them.

in terms of gripes i have one, sirius black dies just before voldemort shows up and his dealt wasn't emotional and that is because his character wasn't developed. the film plays this off as a really emotional moment but us audience members will feel for harry we won't at all feel for sirius.

with a new director at the helm and the constant exploration of our characters and the world they live in, the order of the phoenix is great.

9/10.

spoiler alert i am a great fan of the series i already read all the book and i agree this is one of the best movies in the series maybe even better than the 3rd. which is a relief for the 4th was a disaster in my opinion i mean they were the bloody school champions and they portrayed them as fools. i seems the characters actually went to acting classes for this one. i have some complains though the movie did not capture the end of the book i mean harry was downright furious at sirius death to say the least he was trashing dumbledore's office and was on the verge on going after dumbledore too not seating weeping at his lost. the prophecy was changed and neville's possible involvement. another miss the mirror from sirius is missing and that is important for the last book. i also regret the lost of the comedy part i recall an scene where draco is trying to corner harry and he just replies something like sure the death eaters and voldemort were just warm up practice for you. though i loved the girl playing luna she seemed to be missing her odd artifacts that made her bizarre in the book i do no know odd glasses, strange pendants. however i highly recommend this picture.

i rarely notice the music in films but i did with the last 3 potter films.

john williams music has always fitted well with popular fantasy movies for as long as i can remember and so does his score for harry potter. but he outdid himself with his score for azkaban. his music for that movie really gave it that extra touch of magic (no pun intended) and wonderment and made what was already an excellent movie even better. i would have given him that oscar he was nominated for.

in goblet of fire i too noticed the music but for the wrong reasons. it was too simplistic , repetitive and absolutely made my movie experience a lesser one. just repeating a jingle in a higher tone doesn't raise tension, it jerks me out of my temporary suspension of disbelieve by irritating me.

so when i went to see order i feared they hadn't been able to find someone to fill williams shoes. but i was wrong, the magic is back. nicholas hoopers score is wonderful. at times it too bordered on the simplistic but when it shone, it shone like a full petronas. from the long sighs of the violins at the kiss to the low stabs of the strings during the battle, every major musical piece was full of delightful surprises.

so what about the other stuff? daniel radcliffe impressed me. he and the others kept growing steadily over the years but here i really felt he was a professional actor. emma watsons brows kept distracting me though, keep them steady girl.

like all the others, i thought the fights were excellent but not just for the visual effects. the sound editing during the dumbledore/voldemort fight was spot on. i always appreciate the use of silence and the twirls of dumbledores wand were effective and a wonderful nod to cuarons azkaban. i understand but regret the absence of dobby, specially since deathly hallows where his presence marks important growth for harry's character. but what i really missed was the sacking of hagrid, it would have strengthened harry's feeling of isolation and the (mistaken) absence of order members would help explain his actions. but despite these shortcomings they did get the feeling right with this movie and that is quite an achievement, with all the slashing they had to do. together with azkaban, this is the best potter movie.

this was easily the best movie of the set to this point. they changed a lot from the book but almost all of them worked well in the scope of the film. the acting was the best it's been yet, the plot developed really well, and the darker cinematic vibe was perfect for how harry was feeling throughout the book. honestly, there was really only one negative and it's something they changed from the book so if you haven't read it you might not mind at all. as i said before, "almost all" of the changes worked well. this particular change, however, is being looking over. in my opinion, the most intensely emotional and dramatic sequence in all of the first five books happens in dumbledore's office after they all returned from the ministry of magic. in that moment, the emotions of what took place at the ministry almost literally pour out of the pages. the director felt, i suppose, that this gut wrenching portion of the book was sufficiently covered in a mere 30 seconds of filming where harry and dumbledore barely scratch the surface of what occurred in the actual book. i think this scene should've met the book completely. only then could they have done it justice. without that flaw, however, the movie would've been darn near perfect. i hope the movies continue to get better and better.

i have only been home for about ten minutes and already had the urge to write a review for this film...that's how amazing it is.

i went into the cinema rather curious to see how they were going to squeeze such a vast book into a two hour film. i have to admit that i did not have very high expectations considering how much information was cut out of the fourth film. but they managed it...the film even contained some trivial snippets of the book such as fred and george's extendable ears and umbridge's disgusting collection of kitten plates.

the actors really excel in this film. normally i have a firm favourite out of the trio's performances but out of all honestly they all portrayed their characters without fault.

new faces on the scene will not disappoint you either. evanna was without a doubt a perfect luna as was helena's portrayal of the unhinged bellatrix lestrange.

the special effects in this film are in a league of their own. the climax of the film in the ministry of magic really captures the essence of the book and will leave you buzzing after you have left the cinema because it is just so full of energy.

however if you are a hopeless romantic (like me) it will be the developing romance that you will probably enjoy the most. this film subtly hints towards future couples...ron and hermione of course and even though this is harry and cho's year there are some references to harry and ginny. such as harry's impressed reaction to ginny's powerful reducto spell or ginny's saddened facial expression when harry and cho are together on screen. there is even a growing chemistry between neville and luna, especially in the ministry of magic battle, which is adorable.

like with any film that is based on a novel, cuts have to be made but harry potter and the order of the phoenix really does contain all the significant details that it needs to...if i had to fault the film at all it would be that it did not include hermione kissing ron on the cheek...and that is only because i am a dorky ron and hermione fan...and if you think about it that is a pretty petty fault.

so basically in a long winded nut shell see the film. the effects are brilliant, the acting is amazing and the script really does do the book justice. after all even j. k rowling said herself that this film is her favourite in the series so far so that should be good for everyone else.

with a very impressive directing, flawless acting skills and, precision in technical data ootp deserves accolades or higher ratings when compared to the previous movies of this enchanting series (with an exception of poa).

but when it comes to certain details of events in the book, the movie fails to impress harry potter fans, like for example the st mungo's hospital has been totally eliminated in the movie ,still the most necessary event that occurs in the hospital which is the history of neville's parents is not lost . another problem it faces is the pace at which events happen which happens to be skyrocketing in a baffling yet understandable way (hence those haven't read the book is in for utter confusion) .the visual effects are just beyond comparison with any other movie (fred and george's weasleys fireworks are fantabulous). the final showdown that takes place at the ministry was deliberate but still impressive.

this part of the series was hilarious in many ways and mostly triggered by umbridge (the new teacher for the so told jinxed post of defense against dark arts).taking into account the fact that this book in particular is longest of all the books from the 7part series, the director did a pretty appreciable job. all in all hp fans are in for a visual treat, comparatively less disappointment whereas a fan with no knowledge of the stuff from the book is bound to get confused but still a visual feast awaits.

as a reader of the harry potter books and one who has seen all of the movies, i confess i went into the theater expecting something that was barely mediocre. i was pleasantly surprised.

the order of the phoenix happens to be my favorite book of the series so far, so i planned on seeing it in theaters when it hit. however, after the less-than-stellar performances in goblet of fire, i didn't have much hope. the acting was quite good in this installment. radcliffe portrayed a 15-year-old teenager very well, with his constant mood swings and whirlwind of emotions. i found him very believable and felt as though for once, i could relate to him. he is on a dark and twisting journey, one quite like a lot of people go through in their lives. as mentioned by another user, i was also pleased with michael gambon's performance. although he butchered the character of dumbledore in gof (goblet of fire), i believe that he found dumbledore's true essence in this movie and really allowed himself to become the dumbledore. very impressive.

the plot was very easy to follow as well. i went with a friend to the showing who had only read the first two books and seen only some parts of some movies, and he commented that this was the only one that he could truly follow, and he actually found it quite interesting. i did have to explain some crucial elements to him, but other than that, he understood what was happening, which i've heard is pretty rare for those who see the movies and don't read the books.

as i said before, this movie also happens to be my favorite book in the series, and i was delighted that the movie happened to stay pretty true to the book. it did, however, skip a couple of my favorite scenes (such as "snape's worst memory") and there were many chronological errors and entirely new scenes added. but that is expected with any movie that is adapted from a book. probably with the exception of the first movie, i believe this movie was the truest to the book overall.

overall a 9/10. a truly brilliant movie, and an even more brilliant book. i know that we can look forward to the same with the 6th movie, harry potter and the half-blood prince, for david yates will be directing that movie as well.

admittedly; after hp 4, i was scared that there wouldn't have been any other movies with that scale of magnitude. brilliant dialogs, awesome special effects, and everything that a major fantasy movie should have. now things are changed. you can definitely forget the whole ballet of the fourth movie, and enter into the real harry potter world: a world of solitude,pain and doubt. this movie has a lot of ties with the third installment of the series; the same darkness, the same imminent sense of tragedy; most ultimately, the same sense of doom. without revealing too much of the plot, we can definitely say that we begin to understand harry's personality for what it is for real: traumatized.

the brilliant gothic photography, the soundtrack, magniloquent as always, the whole rhythm of the movie, are definitely involving. the actors, excepts from the usual old glories like gary oldman & co.(from which i didn't expect any less than the usual perfection-as it has been), seem to grow up talented. every performance on a movie is better than the previous one, and i'm just looking forward to the next movie, that should be out in late 2008.

one piece of advice: i've been one of the many to doubt about david yates' capability; mostly, because i'm not from uk, and as such i didn't know his previous works. doesn't matter what the guy did before, with this movie he definitely put his name into the history of cinema. this harry potter saga is growing up as one of the most incredible serial of adventure, and being remembered for the (at least in my opinion) best hp movie so far is definitely something.

okay i'll admit that bookwise, my favorite is the half-blood prince. but seeing as how that one has yet to be made into a movie, i'll talk about the order of the phoenix. i just went and saw the movie today (and i hope to see it in imax sometime). micheal gambon actually made a very good come back as dumbledore unlike in goblet of fire. granted quite a few scenes were cut from the film, they still did a very good job at keeping the story together, so even if you haven't read the books (which no one in my family has except me), you still can understand it. rupert grint as always was excellent as ron, although he could show a little more emotion. emma watson topped it off as hermione being annoying as she sometimes is. and of course daniel radcliffe as harry also gave a good performance. sometimes the look on his was a little creepy as well as intriguing. i also liked robbie coltrane as hagrid, despite him having a relatively small part in the story.

over all except for a few minor complaints about it, they did a great job at getting the story across even with taking out some scenes. the cast was great.

first of all i would like to say that some people who consider the harry potter series the "bible" will be disappointed in the film. i have read all the books and this book is just to long and too complex of a story to condense into a film so don't go into the movie looking for details like tonks' hair being correct or the subtle side plots. they took a great book, over 800 pages, and condensed it into a little over a 2 hour movie... what do you expect? secondly, i would like to say that i really enjoyed this movie. i felt like they gave the movie the feel the book had. dolores umbridge (imelda staunton) and luna lovegood (evanna lynch) were absolutely perfect and brought the characters to life. also harry potter (daniel radcliffe) definitely portrayed the characters feelings and anger throughout the entire movie. i felt like the movie stayed true to the main plot of the book though they had to tweak a lot of details to condense it and make it followable by a person who hasn't read the book.

overall, this was a great movie that i think will have potter readers as well as movie watchers pleasantly surprised with it's action sequences and storyline. it was fairly fast paced, leaving me on the edge of my seat most of the time, and therefore lacked the "feel" of the other movies. what you feel in this movie are the characters. it was definitely more character driven than any of the other movies so far.

again a warning- please don't go into the movie wanting to see the book on screen...it just isn't going to happen.

i loved this movie, it was amazing. absolutely amazing.

there were things about this movie that i didn't like. it never explains the exact details of what happened to neville's parents. that will confuse pretty much everyone who haven't read the books. also, while the music was beautiful, there were a couple of moments where the music didn't fit what was happening. that happened only a few times thankfully.

now onto the good things...

dan radcliffe acting has improved so much. i felt for him each moment he had to feel angry or sad or feel any emotions. i was surprised by emma watson's performance. it's a lot better than goblet of fire. rupert grint is good as always.

the battle scene is amazing. one of the best scenes in the movie. sadly, i didn't get to see it in imax, but it was still amazing.

in the past i have dreaded each release of the potter films and have dragged myself to see the latest instalment. finally with 'hp and the order of the phoenix' we have a film adaptation as true to the book as possible, and a film which in some way captures the imagination, like the books do. perhaps my expectations of previous films were too high, but this flick really stuns you from start to finish and is not overacted, not trivialised and not childish in the same the previous films were. brave mr yates for finally fulfilling the potential of a harry potter film.

9/10
